title: How to Approach Design Questions
description: Learn the right mindset and opening moves for any system design interview question.

data.text: The biggest mistake candidates make is jumping straight to boxes and arrows. A strong opening buys you credibility and gives the interviewer a chance to correct course. Before you draw anything, restate the problem in your own words and confirm who the users are and what success looks like.

data.title: Avoid Premature Design
data.text: Drawing a load balancer in the first thirty seconds signals that you are optimizing before you understand the constraints.

data.title: Opening Moves
items: Restate the problem: So we are designing a URL shortening service like TinyURL, correct?
Identify the users: Who creates links, and who clicks them?
Define scale: Is this for a few hundred requests per day or millions?
List constraints: Are there latency requirements, compliance rules, or legacy integrations?

data.caption: The correct sequence from question to design.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Q[Question] --> R[Restate Problem]
    R --> U[Identify Users]
    U --> S[Define Scale]
    S --> C[List Constraints]
    C --> D[Design]

data.text: Interviewers cannot read your mind. Narrate your reasoning as you work through each step. If you consider a NoSQL database, say why and what trade-off you are making. Out-loud thinking transforms a silent exercise into a conversation, which is exactly what the interviewer is evaluating.

data.title: What to Communicate
items: Your assumptions and why you are making them.
Alternatives you considered and why you rejected them.
Areas where you need more input from the interviewer.
The constraints driving each design decision.

data.title: Opening Checklist
points: Restate the problem before drawing anything.
data.takeaway: A strong opening turns a vague question into a clear design conversation.
